newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday on profit-taking late in the session after receiving a boost at the opening from overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.

The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 21,420 yuan ($2,583) per tonne, losing 150 yuan. It opened at 21,980 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 22,060 and a low of 21,400 yuan per tonne.
August fell 100 to 20,900 yuan per tonne, September 80 to 21,120, October 130 to 21,390, December 80 to 21,500, the January 1997 contract 100 to 21,500 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 177,150 tonnes from 172,250 tonnes.
Zinc raced ahead in London on waves of speculative buying on Friday, sweeping copper, aluminium and nickel with it. LME copper closed the kerb at $2,347, an increase of $82 a tonne.

Three months zinc touched a seven-year peak of $1,625 per tonne in London, bringing gains over the last two days of the week to $100 and the month's rise to $204 or 14 percent. It ended the day $53 higher at $1,624.
This followed news that Chinese smelters were facing a huge short position said to be mostly due in September, having sold forward at around $1,100 a tonne.
Officials of China's central metals production arm China National Nonferrous Metals Corp (CNNC) said on Monday the country's zinc short position on the LME was around 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes.
They said CNNC was considering how it could help the local smelters out of this ditch, and senior leaders were meeting to discuss the matter.
Shanghai copper opened higher and rose further but profit-taking pushed prices down from highs to end near intraday low.
Local traders said many investors took advantage of the Friday LME gains to liquidate their long positions but market sentiment had greatly improved.

"A lot of buyers poured into the market in the morning session but they met strong resistance at the 22,000-yuan level, triggering large amounts of profit-taking late in the session," one trader said.
"But many investors are still optimistic about the later market trend after recent solid gains," he said.
London analysts said they saw the red metal on the LME testing resistance at $2,400 a tonne after last week's constructive close.

This could provide further incentive for the Shanghai metal, a local trader said, adding, though, that prices were riding on the back of zinc, and were not likely to stay up for long as fundamental support was lacking.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices were firm around the 21,000-yuan level due to the strong performance on the futures market, traders said.
Heavy volume indicated the presence of significant amounts of hot money in the metal market, traders said, adding this was likely to cause prices to fluctuate in a wide range in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. August fell 220 yuan to 14,030 yuan per tonne, September 240 to 14,340, October 260 to 14,380, November 280 to 14,350, December 250 to 14,350 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 4,890 tonnes from 7,720 tonnes.
